data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is a consensus-backed session lease with a mandatory linearizable proof-of-absence query against the evidence namespace; it must durably record the lease token, the bound nameset, and the causal timestamp of the absence query.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Consensus unavailability indefinitely blocks reclamation.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Clock skew between lease holder and consensus cluster causes premature expiry.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A delayed network partition allows a zombie workspace holder to commit evidence after proof-of-absence is issued.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The workspace holder maintains a renewable session lease in a consensus-backed lease store. The lease records the exact set of evidence names the workspace may modify. Reclamation is authorized only after a linearizable proof-of-absence query confirms no committed evidence exists for those names under the current lease generation. The protocol durably records the lease grant, the nameset, and the causal timestamp of the proof-of-absence query. Because reclamation cannot proceed without consensus-validated absence, completed evidence cannot be silently displaced by a competing reclamation actor.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
